content: An oro-antral communication is an abnormal opening that forms between the oral cavity and the maxillary sinus. If this opening does not close on its own, it can remain open and become lined with epithelial tissue, eventually developing into an oro-antral fistula. Various treatment methods, both surgical and non-surgical, have been employed to address this condition. Surgical approaches include techniques such as the use of flaps, grafts, and even the re-implantation of third molars. Non-surgical methods involve the use of materials like allogenic grafts or xenografts. The objective of this review was to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of different interventions for treating oro-antral communications and fistulae that arise as a result of dental procedures. To achieve this, a comprehensive search was conducted across multiple databases, including the Cochrane Oral Health Trials Register, CENTRAL, MEDLINE, and Embase, up to May 23, 2018. Additional searches were performed in the US National Institutes of Health Trials Registry (ClinicalTrials.gov) and the World Health Organization International Clinical Trials Registry Platform to identify ongoing trials. No restrictions were applied regarding language or publication date. Reference lists of included and excluded studies were also reviewed to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs). However, quasi-RCTs, cross-over trials, and studies involving oro-antral communications or fistulae related to the Caldwell-Luc procedure or tumor excision were excluded. Two independent reviewers selected the trials, assessed the risk of bias, and extracted data. Risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated for dichotomous outcomes. The overall quality of the evidence was evaluated using the GRADE approach. Only one study met the inclusion criteria for this review. This study compared two surgical techniques: the pedicled buccal fat pad flap and the buccal flap, for the treatment of oro-antral communications. The study included 20 participants, and the risk of bias was unclear. The primary outcome assessed was the successful (complete) closure of the oro-antral communication. The quality of evidence for this outcome was rated as very low. The study found no evidence of a difference between the two interventions in achieving successful closure of the oro-antral communication one month after surgery (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.83 to 1.20). All oro-antral communications in both groups were successfully closed, and no adverse effects related to treatment failure were reported. No other trials evaluating different interventions for oro-antral communications or fistulae caused by dental procedures were identified. In conclusion, the evidence from this single small study was of very low quality and insufficient to determine whether there is a difference in the effectiveness of the pedicled buccal fat pad flap compared to the buccal flap. Both interventions successfully closed the oro-antral communications within one month. There is a need for larger, well-designed RCTs to evaluate various interventions for treating oro-antral communications and fistulae caused by dental procedures to guide clinical practice effectively.
